body.heading: Where in the world is France?
paragraphs: France is a country in Western Europe, which is part of Europe.

body.heading: The capital city
paragraphs: The capital of France is Paris.

body.heading: Words you might hear
paragraphs: The language you will hear most in France is French.

body.heading: Money in your pocket
paragraphs: The money of France is the euro. The euro is shared by many countries in Europe, so the same coins and notes work across borders.

body.heading: How big is France?
paragraphs: France covers about 641,000 square kilometres of land and inland water. That makes it about twice the size of Poland.

body.heading: A fact to wow your friends
paragraphs: The Eiffel Tower was constructed for the 1889 World’s Fair in Paris. When it was finished in 1889, the Eiffel Tower was the tallest structure in the world. Gustave Eiffel's team built it in just over two years.

body.heading: Two places we'd love to visit
paragraphs: Paris is the City of Light: ride up the Eiffel Tower, cruise the Seine past Notre-Dame, and hunt for gargoyles and croissants in between.
Mont Saint-Michel is an abbey on a rocky island that the sea cuts off at high tide — one of the most magical silhouettes in Europe.

body.heading: Think and talk
paragraphs: 1. Find France on a map or globe. Which continent is it on — and can you name a country that sits next to it?
2. Spark and Mango can visit only ONE of the two places in this article. Which should they choose — and what would you pack for the trip?

takeaway: France in one breath: a country in Western Europe, capital Paris, where people speak French and pay with the euro.
